summary.text: Organic chemistry is the study of the structure, properties, and reactions of organic compounds, which are materials containing carbon atoms.
Carbon's valence of four, with single, double, and triple bonds, makes organic compounds structurally diverse and their range of applications enormous.
Organic compounds form the basis of all known life and make up the majority of known chemicals.

items.prompt: In 1828 Friedrich Wöhler made urea, a constituent of urine, from inorganic salts. Why was that important?

options.label: A supposedly organic substance was made without biological starting materials
It proved that urine needs a vital force to form
It showed that inorganic salts are secretly alive
It created the very first synthetic dye

items.explain: It was the first time a substance thought to be organic was synthesized without biological starting materials, an event now generally accepted as disproving vitalism.

items.prompt: The concept of chemical structure was a crucial breakthrough. What did its developers propose about carbon atoms?

options.label: Carbon atoms are always bonded to oxygen
Carbon atoms cannot link to one another
Four-bonded carbon atoms can link to each other into a carbon lattice
Carbon atoms are held together by a vital force

items.explain: Kekulé and Couper suggested that tetravalent carbon atoms could link to each other to form a carbon lattice.

items.prompt: How did a failed attempt to make quinine boost interest in organic chemistry?

options.label: Perkin proved vitalism wrong with the attempt
Perkin accidentally made a dye whose financial success made it widely known
Perkin made quinine from urine instead
Perkin's failed attempt closed the field to students

items.explain: While trying to manufacture quinine, Perkin accidentally produced a dye, and its financial success greatly increased interest in organic chemistry.

items.prompt: Why did plant-sourced indigo production fall sharply between 1897 and 1914?

options.label: Plant indigo was shown to be toxic to wearers
Wöhler's urea synthesis got it outlawed
The crops failed all over the world in those years
Adolf von Baeyer's synthetic methods cut the need for it

items.explain: Production of indigo from plant sources dropped from 19,000 tons in 1897 to 1,000 tons by 1914 thanks to the synthetic methods developed by Adolf von Baeyer.

items.prompt: Why might biochemistry be regarded as essentially a branch of organic chemistry?

options.label: Most compounds in living organisms are carbon compounds
Most living organisms are made of metals
Biochemistry was named before organic chemistry
Both fields were founded by the same person

items.explain: The majority of chemical compounds in biological organisms are carbon compounds, so the association is so close that biochemistry might be regarded as essentially a branch of organic chemistry.

items.prompt: How did the discovery of petroleum affect organic chemistry?

options.label: It showed that oil needs a vital force
It moved the field's focus to inorganic salts
The petrochemical industry it spurred drove the field's growth
It made total synthesis unnecessary

items.explain: The discovery of petroleum and the development of the petrochemical industry spurred the development of organic chemistry, enabling products such as plastics and synthetic rubber.
